family_correction.note: the within-cell grid search is already absorbed by the permutation test; this corrects the family of cells on top of it

pre_registrations.statement: On the one arm with a real allocation signal (HumanEval `error`, Week 12 ROC 0.706, p=1e-4), repair success is monotone non-decreasing in P(pass) RANK. There is no interior sweet spot in the percentile reading.
pre_registrations.falsifier: some interior quintile's hit rate exceeds the top quintile's by more than that quintile's Wilson half-width

pre_registrations.statement: The user's proposed raw band [0.40, 0.55) beats the `inverted` ordering at matched ATTEMPTS on both HumanEval context arms, and survives a label permutation test at alpha=0.05.
pre_registrations.falsifier: the band is <= inverted at every INFORMATIVE attempt-matched point (every point below its prefix-equivalence crossover, past which the two orderings cover the same set by construction), OR its ordering margin fails a label-permutation null at alpha=0.05 at every such point, OR it does not beat the region ABOVE it (Fisher p >= 0.05) -- on a monotone gradient any top region beats the cohort average, so beating the average is not evidence of a band

pre_registrations.statement: Excluding the bottom of the distribution is the robust win: attempting only p >= 0.10 retains >= 60% of Repair-All's passes for <= 50% of its calls, on both HumanEval context arms.
pre_registrations.falsifier: either retention < 60% or call share > 50% on either arm

pre_registrations.statement: PREDICTED TO FAIL, and pre-registered as such so the null is publishable: a band chosen OUT OF FOLD by the pilot rule beats the `inverted` ordering out of sample. Two explanations are not separated by this test and both must be reported: bands may be unlearnable at this cohort size, and `select_band_on` prices a band without regard to its SIZE, so a narrow well-priced band cannot fill a budget it was selected to spend.
pre_registrations.falsifier: the pilot-selected band is <= inverted at >= 3 of the 4 sub-full budgets

pre_registrations.statement: Band the ESCALATION, not the first attempt. On the coordinates the context-free `none` arm fails, escalating only where P(pass) >= 0.20 captures >= 40% of the context-rescuable coordinates using <= 35% of the escalation attempts.
pre_registrations.falsifier: capture < 40% of rescues, or attempt share > 35%

pre_registrations.statement: Cohort dependence, DESCRIPTIVE ONLY: the band advantage is present on HumanEval and absent on MBPP. n=2 cohorts cannot identify the near-miss mechanism the user hypothesises; a third cohort is the test, and it is the same third cohort Week 12's open item (1) asks for.
pre_registrations.falsifier: the oracle band beats `inverted` on MBPP by more than it does on HumanEval (which would make the pattern not cohort-ordered)

observed.note: descriptive only; n=2 cohorts cannot identify the near-miss mechanism, and the MBPP `error` arm carries 10 positives so its null excludes only a LARGE effect

pre_registrations.verdict: not falsified, but UNINFORMATIVE at this granularity (gap of one repair on a one-repair statistic; do not report as confirmation of cohort dependence)
